description: Named for a legendary princess, Kumari Ella is a serene four-meter waterfall in Hewahinna. Formed by the convergence of mountain streams, it feeds into the Kelani River. Despite its small scale, the site remains a prominent landmark and a popular nature escape near Colombo.

The Ella Uda Ella Falls (Kahana Ella) takes its water from the Kodikande Mountain and the Koswatte Canal network, which flows through rock and tree-lined valleys, before cascading from a cliff at the point of the fall. A species of fish, known locally as mahseer (Tor khudree),

The 15m high Ranmudu Ella Falls in Thunmodara is situated in a tributary of the Wakganga River, and the waters feed the Kelani River. The fall is a victim of its success. Due to its popularity, especially at weekends, the surrounding ecosystem is under threat from large numbers of trampling visitors
Although the published height of the waterfall is 10 meters, it is said that the waterfall is 15-20 meters. There is no proper access to the waterfall and it’s a difficult climb to reach the fall
Galle Face Green is a 5 ha (12 acres) ocean-side urban park, which stretches for 500 m (1,600 ft) along the coast, in the heart of Colombo, the financial and business capital of Sri Lanka.

Viharamahadevi Park is one of the ancientest parks and is adored by tourists and visitors for its relaxing atmosphere, golden Buddha statue, cultural and historical essence, beautiful views, and children’s activities.

Diyatha Uyana is Colombo’s best-kept family secret. Located along the Diyawanna Oya lake in Battaramulla (near Parliament), this beautifully maintained park and market area is where Colombo families spend their weekends — and for good reason.

Seethawaka Wet zone Botanic Gardens is the 5th Botanic Garden of the Department of National Botanic Gardens and the first botanic garden established solely for the conservation of wet zone flora in Sri Lanka.

The National Museum of Natural History is a museum that covers the natural heritage of Sri Lanka. The museum is located closer to the National Museum of Colombo. It was established on September 23, 1986, and became only one museum in Sri Lanka that represents natural history and natural heritage.

Independence Memorial Hall is a national monument in Sri Lanka built for the commemoration of the independence of Sri Lanka from British rule, with the restoration of full governing responsibility to a Ceylonese-elected legislature on 4 February 1948.

The Old Colombo Dutch Hospital is considered to be the oldest building in the Colombo Fort area dating back to the Dutch colonial era in Sri Lanka. It is now a heritage building and a shopping and dining precinct.

We were quite taken aback at the elaborate stonework that decorated the ruins of the Barandi Kovila .

As we walked through the gate installed by the  Archaeological Department, we could see three distinct terraces built one upon the other. The third and the upper terrace housed the ruins of the Barandi Kovila – a square structure with stone pillars.
Dehiwala Beach is a calm, less-crowded coastal stretch located in the Dehiwala-Mount Lavinia area, just south of Colombo, Sri Lanka.
Galle Face Beach is a popular urban coastal strip and public park located in the heart of Colombo, Sri Lanka.
Wellawatta Beach is an urban coastal strip in Colombo 6, Sri Lanka, known for its local community atmosphere, sunset views, and active railway line running parallel to the shore

An accessible space that is a sanctuary from the hustle and bustle of Colombo, a place that is family and pet friendly, with a cafe and bar, private swimmable beach, and a host of unique activities and events for all age

Mount Lavinia Beach sits roughly 12 kilometres south of central Colombo along the coastal Galle Road, making it the most convenient stretch of sand for visitors staying in or passing through the capital. Unlike the resort beaches further south, it offers an authentic slice of Sri Lankan coastal life — fishing boats at dawn, beach vendors by midday, and long amber sunsets that draw locals and travellers alike.

Beddagana Wetland Park provides a home for a wide variety of wetland birds, butterflies, dragonflies, fishes and various animals amongst wetland vegetation and tranquil ponds as well as the Diyawanna Lake. This is a ‘live demonstration’ that aims to underscore wetlands’ importance to the overall ‘livability’ of cities such as Colombo.

Gangaramaya Temple is one of the most important temples in Colombo, Sri Lanka, being a mix of modern architecture and cultural essence. Located on the Beira Lake, it was completed in the late 19th century

Construction of the Jami-Ul-Alfar Mosque commenced in 1908 and the building was completed in 1909.[2][3] The mosque was commissioned by the local Indian Muslim community, based in Pettah, to fulfill their required five-times-daily prayer and Jummah on Fridays.

St. Anthony's Shrine is a Catholic church in the Archdiocese of Colombo in Sri Lanka. The church is located at Kochchikade, Kotahena, Colombo 13, and is dedicated to Saint Anthony of Padua. The church is designated a national shrine and minor basilica.

Halpe Estate is a settlement in Western Province, Sri Lanka, at 51 m elevation. The nearest larger town is Hanwella Ihala, 8 km to the northwest. The national capital Colombo is 32 km to the west. The nearest airport is Ratmalana Airport, 27 km away.
The Imbula Kanda Temple (ඉඹුලකන්ද රජමහා විහාරය) is located in Homagama, Sri Lanka, sitting on top of the Imbula Kanda hill

Henarathgoda Botanical Garden, also known as Gampaha Botanical Garden, is one of the six botanical gardens in Sri Lanka. The botanical garden is situated on the Gampaha-Minuwangoda main road, approximately 450 m away from Gampaha railway station. It is about 29 km from Sri Lanka's commercial capital of Colombo.

It was captured by Dutch forces commanded by Philip Lucasz, in February 1640.[1] The Portuguese made several attempts to retake it before they were successful in December 1643. They then strengthened the fortifications and managed to defend the fort until it was recaptured by the Dutch under the command of François Caron, in January 1644
The Hamilton Canal, also known as the Dutch Canal, is a historic 14.5-kilometer (9-mile) waterway in Sri Lanka that connects the Kelani River estuary in Colombo to the Negombo Lagoon and Puttalam.

Negombo Beach is a famous west-coast beach in Sri Lanka, located about 10 km from Bandaranaike International Airport and 38 km north of Colombo. Nicknamed "Little Rome" for its heavy Roman Catholic influence and historic churches, it is a popular first or last stop for travelers.

Negombo Lagoon is a large estuarine lagoon in Negombo, south-west Sri Lanka. The lagoon is fed by a number of small rivers and the Hamilton Canal. It is linked to the sea by a narrow channel to the north, near Negombo city.

Muthurajawela Marsh is Sri Lanka's largest saline coastal peat bog, located just south of Negombo and about 30 km north of Colombo. The name translates to "Swamp of Royal Treasure," reflecting its immense ecological and historical value.

The temple has often been associated with the rise and fall of Sri Lanka, with the popular saying that as the Kelaniya temple rose, Sri Lanka rose and as it fell, the country and its administration fell. It has thus had a deep association with the political powers of the country. As such, the temple is frequently visited by politicians both government and opposition.
St. Mary's Church is a landmark edifice, a Roman Catholic church in the heart of Negombo. It is one of the largest Catholic church in Sri Lanka.

King Sri Sangabo (251–253 CE) is remembered in the chronicles and ancient literature of Sri Lanka as one of the most pious  Buddhist rulers in the island’s history. Closely associated with his memory is Attanagalla Rajamaha Viharaya, one of the most renowned ancient royal temples of the country. The temple is located in the Western Province, about 45 kilometers (28 miles) northeast of Colombo.

Pilikuththuwa Raja Maha Vihara is an ancient Cave temple situated in Pilikuththuwa, Sri Lanka. It is located on the Gampaha - Wathurugama road approximately 3.8 km away from the Miriswatta junction and 1.6 km from the ancient Buddhist temple, Maligatenna Raja Maha Vihara.

Warana Raja Maha Vihara is an ancient Buddhist temple situated in Thihariya, Gampaha District, Sri Lanka. The temple is located approximately 5 km away from the Colombo - Kandy highway. Currently this temple has been recognized as an archaeological protected site in Gampaha District by Archaeological department.

Hidden off the Talduwa–Meewitigammana road, Goraka Ella is a quiet cascade reached through paddy fields and village footpaths. With rocky tiers, seasonal pools, and a peaceful rural setting, it rewards adventurous visitors who seek solitude beyond the usual tourist trails.

A unique feature of its geography is its boundary layout: it is bordered directly by the main Veyangoda – Ruwanwella Road on one side (providing easy roadside accessibility) and a natural flowing water stream on the other side (Camping site)

Thudugala Ella is a two-tiered, 14-meter waterfall set within a historic 400-hectare estate in Kalutara. Famous for its natural swimming pools, giant pus creepers, and rare endemic biodiversity, it features a unique tunnel path. Despite nearby oil palm cultivation, it remains a serene sanctuary for nature lovers and bathers alike.

Pahanthuda literally refers to the wick of a small clay lamp, particularly the type traditionally used in temples. The waterfall derives its name from the shape of its base pool, which resembles a clay lamp, while the falling water itself is said to resemble the wick of the lamp

The Magical Sapphire Natural Pool is a rapidly growing attraction located within a 9-acre area on the Crurie Estate in Galkaduwa, Pahala Neboda, within the Kalutara District of Sri Lanka. It features a calm, refreshing bathing spot formed by a natural flowing stream winding through rock formations and enhanced by structured elements like stone steps, walkways, and a small waterfall. Surrounded by lush tropical greenery, it offers a peaceful and clean environment that appeals to nature lovers and travelers looking for a quick escape

Richmond Castle is an Edwardian mansion, located near Kalutara. Built between 1900 and 1910, it was formally the country seat of Mudaliyar Don Arthur de Silva Wijesinghe Siriwardena. The building is currently owned by the Public Trustee and open to the public.

Fa Hien Cave, also known locally as Pahiyangala Cave (Fa-Hien Lena), is one of the most critical prehistoric and religious sites in South Asia. Located in the remote village of Yatagampitiya near Bulathsinhala within Sri Lanka's Kalutara District, it stands out as the largest natural rock shelter in South Asia. The massive limestone structure features a semi-circular hollow entrance soaring roughly 175 feet high, capable of accommodating up to 3,000 people simultaneously.

Kalutara Bodhiya is one of the most sacred and visually striking Buddhist landmarks in Sri Lanka. Situated just 43 km south of Colombo along the Galle-Colombo main road (A2), it sits spectacularly on the southern bank of the Kalu Ganga (Black River) right where the river meets the Indian Ocean

Kechimalai Mosque (officially Ketchchimalai Grand Mosque or Ketchimala Dharga Shareef) is one of the oldest and most historically significant Islamic sites in Sri Lanka. Perched beautifully on a rocky, palm-fringed headland at the edge of the Beruwala fishing harbor, this striking white landmark marks the precise location where the ancestors of the Sri Lankan Moor community first arrived on the island

Kande Viharaya in Aluthgama is a historic and deeply revered hilltop Buddhist temple famed for housing one of the tallest seated Buddha statues in the world. Officially recognized as an archaeological site by the Sri Lankan government, the temple gets its name—Kande Vihara (Mountain Temple)—from its scenic location atop a hill near the coastal town of Aluthgama and adjacent to Bentota

Kodigahakanda Sanctuary sits quietly in the lowland forests of Sri Lanka's Southern Province, a short drive from the town of Horana. It is one of those places that rewards unhurried visitors — a working conservation area rather than a polished tourist attraction, where the emphasis falls firmly on ecology, research, and wildlife rather than infrastructure or crowds.

waterfall has a height of approximately 10 meters. From a distance, its cascading water os said to resemble the delicate veil of a bride. The surrounding terrain is dotted with rounded granite boulders that have been shaped over time by natural weathering processes.
Huluganga Falls is a striking 75-meter-high waterfall located in Huluganga Town, approximately 30 kilometers from Kandy in Sri Lanka's Central Province

The Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya is the largest and most spectacular botanical garden in Sri Lanka, widely considered one of the finest in Asia. Spanning 147 acres (59 hectares), it is situated just 5.5 km west of Kandy and is uniquely bounded on three sides by a massive, sweeping loop of the Mahaweli River

Since the spelling varies between Embekke and Embekka, it is the exact same 14th-century temple complex located 15 km southwest of Kandy that is universally famous for housing the finest medieval wood carvings in Sri Lanka.

Gadaladeniya Viharaya (originally named Saddharmatilaka Vihara or Dharma Kirthi Viharaya) is a magnificent 14th-century Buddhist monastery and one of the largest ancient rock temples in Sri Lanka. Perched atop a scenic stone outcrop known as Diggala, it sits in Pilimathalawa, roughly 12.5 km west of Kandy city

Arthur's Seat, also widely known as the Kandy View Point, is the definitive lookout platform offering the iconic postcard panorama of Sri Lanka’s hill capital. Situated along Rajapihilla Mawatha southwest of Kandy Lake, this scenic roadside deck sits roughly 550 meters (1,800 feet) above sea level

The Hanthana Mountain Range is a breathtakingly scenic, emerald-green mountain chain rising directly southwest of Kandy city. Comprising seven distinct peaks—the highest being Uura Kanda at around 1,200 meters (3,800 feet)—this protected environmental zone is legendary for its romanticized role in local Sinhala music and poetry

Ambuluwawa Tower is a striking, surreal architectural marvel and the centerpiece of Sri Lanka’s first official multi-religious sanctuary. Rising atop Ambuluwawa Mountain at 1,112 meters (3,650 feet) above sea level near the historic town of Gampola, this 48-meter (157-foot) white spiral tower looks like something out of a fantasy novel

Rathna Ella (translating to "Field of Gems" waterfall) is a majestic, hidden natural wonder tucked away in the village of Hasalaka, Sri Lanka. Fed by the pristine Hasalaka Oya stream originating from the Knuckles Mountain Range, this breathtaking waterfall stands 101 meters (331 feet) tall, ranking officially as the 14th highest waterfall in Sri Lanka and widely noted as one of the widest on the island

The Dothalugala Nature Trail is a highly rewarding, circular trekking path hidden within the southern buffer zone of the Knuckles Conservation Forest. Starting from the Deanston Knuckles Information Centre near Hunnasgiriya, this 5.8 to 6-kilometer trail loops around the slopes of the majestic Dothalugala Mountain, rising into high-altitude ecosystems that showcase the incredible biodiversity of this UNESCO World Heritage site

Hatale Mini World’s End, locally known as Hatale Pathana, is a breathtaking viewpoints and nature escape situated in the Kandy District, Sri Lanka. Perched at an elevation of roughly 3,500 feet above sea level, this hidden gem offers panoramic vistas of the mist-laden Knuckles Mountain Range and the sweeping valleys below

Bellwood, widely famous for the Belwood 360° Viewpoint (and the adjacent Muthukeliyawa Lake), is a stunning hill-country destination nestled in the Galaha–Talatuoya region of the Kandy District, Sri Lanka. Sitting roughly 2,900 feet above sea level, it has quickly gained a reputation among locals as "Little New Zealand" due to its sweeping green grasslands, rolling tea terraces, pine forests, and cool, mist-laden climate

Rathnagiriya View Point (often spelled Ratnagiri) is a spectacular, lesser-known mountain vantage point situated near Gomara village in the Panwila region of the Kandy District, Sri Lanka. Perched beautifully along the foothills of the Knuckles Mountain Range, it serves as an excellent, manageable alternative for hikers who want sweeping panoramic mountain views without undertaking an exhaustive, multi-day trek to the highest peaks.

Kandy Lake, locally revered as Kiri Muhuda (the Sea of Milk), is a historic, man-made reservoir beautifully framing the heart of the hill capital, Kandy, Sri Lanka. Spanning roughly 47 acres (19 hectares) with a maximum depth of 60 feet (18.5 meters), it stands as one of the country's most iconic cultural landmarks.

Udawattakele Forest Reserve, locally known as Udawatta Kele Sanctuary, is a historic, 104-hectare (257-acre) tropical rainforest sanctuary perched on a hill ridge directly behind the Temple of the Tooth Relic.

place_name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
description: The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, locally known as Sri Dalada Maligawa, is a highly revered Buddhist temple situated in the heart of the historic city of Kandy, Sri Lanka. Located inside the Royal Palace Complex of the former Kingdom of Kandy, the temple houses the sacred left canine tooth relic of Gautama Buddha. It stands as a pinnacle of Sri Lankan heritage, architectural brilliance, and spirituality, attracting pilgrims and global travelers alike.

The Bahirawakanda Vihara Buddha Statue, housed within the Sri Maha Bodhi Viharaya, is a towering iconic monument that dominates the skyline of Kandy, Sri Lanka. Standing at an impressive 88 feet (26.8 meters) tall, this brilliant white colossal statue depicts Lord Buddha seated in the Dhyana Mudra (posture of deep meditation). Perched atop the Bahirawa Kanda (Gnome or Devil's Mountain) hill just 2 kilometers from the city center, it is visible from almost everywhere in Kandy.

Yahangala, widely known as Bed Rock Mountain, is a massive, distinctive mountain peak situated in the Kalugala village of Udadumbara, within the Kandy District, Sri Lanka. Standing at an elevation of 1,220 meters (4,003 feet) above sea level, it forms a striking, block-shaped fortress on the southeastern edge of the Knuckles Mountain Range.

Welangolla Pathana (වෙලන්ගොල්ල පතන) is a stunning, high-altitude montane grassland plain situated in the Kalugala area of Udadumbara, within the Kandy District, Sri Lanka. Nestled along the eastern ridges of the Knuckles Mountain Range, this breathtaking plateau is best known as the vital gateway and staging ground for conquering the iconic Yahangala (Bed Rock Mountain)

Kehelpathdoruwegala (often simplified as Kehelpathdoruwa), famously dubbed the "Little Everest of Sri Lanka", is a soaring mountain peak situated in the Udadumbara region of the Kandy District, Sri Lanka. Rising between 1,400 and 1,529 meters (4,593 to 5,016 feet) above sea level, it stands directly adjacent to the famous Yahangala (Bed Rock Mountain) on the southeastern edge of the Knuckles Mountain Range.

Kanaviddagala Mountain (කනවිද්දාගල) is an exceptionally steep and thrilling peak located in Kalugala village, Udadumbara, within the eastern sector of the Knuckles Mountain Range, Sri Lanka. Rising along the route toward the famous Yahangala and Welangolla Pathana region, it is widely regarded by local adventurers as one of the most challenging and vertical scrambles in the Kandy district

Sera Ella (සේර ඇල්ල) is a magnificent 10-meter (33-foot) twin-cascade waterfall tucked away in the remote Pothatawela village near Laggala, in the Matale District (Riverston / Knuckles region) of Sri Lanka. Formed by the Puwakpitiya River joining the Thelgamu Oya, it is celebrated as one of the most picturesque and unusual waterfalls in the Knuckles mountain range highlands.

Bambarakiri Ella (බඹරකිරි ඇල්ල) is a scenic, multi-tiered 10-meter waterfall set within the lush evergreen forests of the Knuckles mountain range, located roughly 16 km from Matale town in the Central Province, Sri Lanka. Positioned along the primary mountain road leading toward Riverston, it serves as an iconic and easily accessible roadside stop for travelers exploring the central highlands.

Popham's Arboretum is Sri Lanka’s only dry zone arboretum, located just 5 kilometers outside of Dambulla along the Kandalama Road. Originally established in 1963 by British planter and naval officer Sam Popham, this 34.5-acre sanctuary stands as a remarkable monument to Assisted Natural Regeneration (ANR)

Sigiriya Rock, also known as Sinhagiri (Lion Rock), is a towering 180-meter-high ancient rock fortress and UNESCO World Heritage site located in the northern Matale District near Dambulla, Sri Lanka. Rising dramatically above the surrounding central plains, this massive volcanic plug serves as one of the country's most iconic cultural landmarks.

Nalanda Gedige is an ancient stone temple near Matale, Sri Lanka that is famously considered the island's geographical center point. Constructed entirely out of dry-jointed granite blocks without mortar between the 8th and 10th centuries, it stands as one of the country's most compelling archaeological mysteries due to its highly unique, hybrid architectural design

Pidurangala Rock is a massive, rugged volcanic outcrop located just 1 kilometer north of Sigiriya Rock. While Sigiriya is famous for its royal fortress and highly manicured gardens, Pidurangala offers a vastly different, more adventurous experience. Surrounded by dense jungle, it features a deep-rooted history as a 5th-century Buddhist monastery and stands as the absolute best viewpoint to witness Sigiriya Rock in its full, dramatic glory.

Riverston is a breathtaking mountain gap and peak situated at an elevation of 1,424 meters in the Matale District of Central Province, Sri Lanka, serving as a dramatic northern gateway to the Knuckles Mountain Range. Known for its wildly shifting microclimates, strong winds (Hulang Kapolla), and sweeping cloud forests, it offers an off-the-beaten-path alternative to Sri Lanka's more crowded southern hill country

Dambulla Cave Temple, also known as the Golden Temple of Dambulla, is the largest and best-preserved cave temple complex in Sri Lanka. Towering 160 meters over the surrounding central plains, this UNESCO World Heritage Site dates back to the 1st century BCE. It was founded by King Valagamba, who transformed these natural caverns into a magnificent place of worship out of gratitude after finding refuge here during his political exile.

Aluvihare Rock Temple (also called Matale Alu Viharaya) is a highly revered ancient cave temple nestled among massive granite boulders in the Matale District, about 30 kilometers north of Kandy. Dating back to the 3rd century BCE, its architecture is visually unique because the shrines are "pouched" inside natural rock clefts formed by towering boulders rather than carved into a single flat cliff face

Sri Muthumariamman Temple, also known as Sri Muthumari Amman Kovil, is a highly vibrant Dravidian-style Hindu shrine situated right in the heart of Matale, Sri Lanka. Dedicated to Mariamman—the goddess of rain, fertility, and protection against diseases—the temple's prefix "muthu" translates to "pearl," reflecting the goddess's pristine maternal blessings. Sitting prominently along the A9 Kandy-Jaffna highway, it serves as a spectacular explosion of South Indian color and a major spiritual center for both Hindu and Buddhist devotees in the region

Trekking to Thunhisgala requires a multi-hour journey through incredibly raw ecosystems, transitioning from sprawling tea plantations into dense, mossy montane cloud forests and abandoned, spice-scented cardamom estates.

The Knuckles Infinity Pool is a stunning, naturally formed rock pool hidden deep inside the virgin cloud forests of the Knuckles Conservation Forest. Fed by an icy mountain stream, the water overflows over a sheer granite ledge, creating a breathtaking, borderless visual effect that looks out across the vast mountain valleys below

Lakegala (literally translating to the "Rock of Lanka") is a spectacular, sharp granite monolith rising 1,310 meters high within the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Knuckles Mountain Range. Famously dubbed the "Matterhorn of Sri Lanka" due to its distinctive, near-perfect triangular pyramid shape, it stands as a legendary icon along the border of the Kandy and Matale districts

Lover's Leap Waterfall is a striking 30-meter-tall (98 feet) cascade tucked away in the misty hills of Hawa Eliya, just 3 kilometers outside Nuwara Eliya town center. Fed by clear streams originating from the slopes of Pidurutalagala (Sri Lanka's highest mountain), this beautiful waterfall serves as the town's closest natural escape and contributes to the area's drinking water supply

Devon Falls, affectionately dubbed the "Veil of the Valley," is one of Sri Lanka’s most striking and popular waterfalls. Plunging 97 meters (318 feet) down a distinct, three-tiered "geological staircase," it ranks as the 19th highest waterfall on the island. Situated at an elevation of 1,140 meters above sea level in the Dimbula region of the Nuwara Eliya District, it is beautifully framed by rolling emerald tea estates

St. Clair’s Falls, universally celebrated as the "Little Niagara of Sri Lanka," is one of the widest and most majestic waterfalls on the island. Perched at an altitude of 1,198 meters above sea level in the Nuwara Eliya District, this iconic landmark runs through the rolling, emerald terrains of the St. Clair Tea Estate just 3 kilometers west of Talawakele along the Avissawella-Hatton-Nuwara Eliya (A7) Highway

Ramboda Falls is a majestic 109-meter-tall (358 feet) tiered cascade situated in the Pussellawa/Kothmale region of the Nuwara Eliya District. Ranking proudly as the 11th highest waterfall in Sri Lanka, it sits at an elevation of 945 meters above sea level along the Kandy-Nuwara Eliya (A5) highway at the iconic Ramboda Pass

Victoria Park is a beautifully manicured, 27-acre urban public oasis located right in the heart of Nuwara Eliya, Sri Lanka, directly adjacent to the iconic colonial Nuwara Eliya Post Office. Originally used as an experimental crop research field for the nearby Hakgala Botanical Garden, it was formally established and named in 1897 to commemorate Queen Victoria’s Diamond Jubilee. Today, it stands as one of the most meticulously maintained urban green spaces in South Asia, characterized by its distinct "Little England" colonial atmosphere

Hakgala Botanical Garden is Sri Lanka’s second-largest botanical haven and the highest-altitude public garden on the island. Nestled on the terraced slopes of the massive Hakgala Rock (2,200m) at an elevation of 1,745 meters above sea level, this 28-hectare paradise overlooks the sweeping plains of the Uva Valley

Pidurutalagala, also known as Mount Pedro in English, is the highest mountain in Sri Lanka. Rising proudly to an elevation of 2,524 meters (8,281 feet) above sea level, it stands just north-northeast of the misty hill station of Nuwara Eliya. It is recognized globally as the island's sole "ultra-prominent peak" due to its massive topographic prominence.

Horton Plains National Park is a breathtaking, 12.2-square-mile (31 km²) protected reserve nestled in the central highlands of Sri Lanka. Perched on a high-altitude plateau between 2,100 and 2,300 meters above sea level, this UNESCO World Heritage Site is an ethereal wilderness characterized by mist-shrouded cloud forests, windswept montane grasslands (patanas), and exceptionally rich, endemic biodiversit

Gregory Lake (also known as Gregory Reservoir) is a picturesque 225-acre man-made lake situated right in the heart of Nuwara Eliya, Sri Lanka. Established in 1873 by British Governor Sir William Gregory, this expansive body of water was created by damming the Thalagala River to transform a swampy bog into a functional reservoir.

Seetha Amman Temple (also known as Seetha Eliya Seethai Amman Thirukkovil) is a highly revered Hindu shrine located in the small village of Seetha Eliya, roughly 5 kilometers southeast of Nuwara Eliya. Built in the classic, colorful South Indian Tamil architectural style, it holds monumental religious significance as the world's only temple dedicated explicitly to Goddess Sita, making it the absolute centerpiece of the Sri Lanka Ramayana Trail.
Malamura Ella Waterfall is situated in the Galle district. Its height has not been recorded. It is a calm place with beautiful surroundings and is ideal to have a bath in.

Nestled in the lush countryside of Elpitiya, Andahelena Ella is a peaceful natural escape surrounded by tropical greenery and rural charm. It is a perfect stop for travellers seeking a quiet, authentic experience away from the busy tourist routes.

Brahmana Ella is a scenic 54m waterfall set within the lush rainforest of southern Sri Lanka, featuring a refreshing natural pool at its base. Surrounded by rich vegetation and local folklore, it offers visitors a tranquil nature experience away from the main tourist routes.

Sarasanda Waterfall is a scenic natural attraction surrounded by lush greenery, offering a peaceful setting for visitors of all ages. Its family-friendly environment makes it a suitable destination for travellers visiting with children.

Gal Oruwa Ella is a striking 30-metre waterfall surrounded by the lush rainforest landscape of Lankagama. Known for its distinctive boat-shaped rock formation and powerful cascade, it offers visitors a unique natural attraction within the Sinharaja region.
Mahamodara Beach Park & Marine Walk is a quiet, scenic coastal park located in Galle on Sri Lanka's southern coast, offering a serene escape with a well-maintained walking path and sunset views

Dharmapala Park is a peaceful urban park in Galle, offering visitors a pleasant green space to relax and enjoy a break from the surrounding city. Its open surroundings and accessible location make it a convenient stop for families and travellers exploring Galle.

The Historical Mansion Museum is the largest private museum in Sri Lanka, beautifully housed inside a restored 17th-century Dutch colonial house. Located on Leyn Baan Street within the UNESCO-listed Galle Fort, this unique attraction operates as a massive "Aladdin's cave" of historical artifacts, antiques, and colonial curiosities curated by a long-time local family

The National Museum of Galle, also called the Galle National Museum, is an engaging history museum situated on Church Street within the UNESCO-listed Galle Fort, Sri Lanka. Established on March 31, 1986, it provides a concise yet fascinating look into the anthropological, colonial, and trade history of the southern province

Galle Dutch Fort, located on the southwest coast of Sri Lanka, is a remarkably preserved UNESCO World Heritage site. Initially built by the Portuguese in 1588, it was extensively fortified and expanded by the Dutch starting in 1649. Today, it stands as the largest remaining fortress in Asia built by European occupiers, functioning as a vibrant, living historic town where colonial architecture seamlessly blends with modern boutique cafes, shops, and homes.

Martin Wickramasinghe Folk Museum, situated along the Galle-Matara main road in Koggala, Southern Province, Sri Lanka, is a massive cultural repository dedicated to the "Father of Modern Sinhala Literature". Spanning a serene seven-acre garden, this complex beautifully pairs the 200-year-old ancestral home of the legendary writer with an expansive folk museum showcasing over a thousand artifacts of traditional rural Sri Lankan life

Kalubovitiyangala, also popularly known as Kalubovitiyana Kanda, is a spectacular mountain peak located in the Matara District of the Southern Province, Sri Lanka. Rising to an elevation of roughly 2,200 to 2,400 feet above sea level, it stands as the highest mountain peak in the Matara district and sits immediately adjacent to the borders of the lush Sinharaja Rainforest Complex.

Unawatuna Beach is arguably Sri Lanka's most famous and highly developed banana-shaped golden sand beach, stretching along a protected bay in the Southern Province. Located just 5 kilometers southeast of the historic city of Galle, this bustling coastal strip is a favorite for travelers seeking a lively atmosphere, calm swimming waters, and an abundant mix of beachfront restaurants and vibrant bars

Jungle Beach is a stunning, secluded twin-cove hideaway tucked along the densely forested slopes of the Rumassala Headland in the Southern Province. Located just a short hop across the bay from the bustling main resort strip of Unawatuna Beach and roughly 6.5 km from the historic Galle Fort, it offers a wilder, more serene alternative to the wide, commercialized tourist beaches nearby.

Hikkaduwa Beach, located along the southwest coast in the Galle District, Southern Province, is widely celebrated as Sri Lanka’s original resort town. Spanning a highly developed coastline, it seamlessly combines a protected Marine National Park (Coral Sanctuary) directly offshore with an energetic surf culture and a legendary beachfront strip lined with cafes, bars, and guesthouses.

Bentota Beach, famously celebrated as the "Golden Mile" of Sri Lanka's southwest coast, is a world-class resort strip located in the Galle District, Southern Province. Sandwiched beautifully on a narrow peninsula between the turquoise waves of the Indian Ocean and the mirror-flat mangrove backwaters of the Bentota Ganga (River) lagoon, it stands as the ultimate capital for both absolute relaxation and adrenaline-pumping water sports

Angiri Ella (ආංගිරි ඇල්ල) is a stunning, lesser-known waterfall hidden away in the Hiniduma region of the Galle District, Southern Province, Sri Lanka. Tucked near the borders of the lush Kanneliya-Nakiadeniya-Sinharaja rainforest ecosystem, this off-the-beaten-path cascade is a local favorite for its pristine, untouched environment and tranquil natural pools

Kaludiya Pokuna (කළුදිය පොකුණ), meaning "Black Water Pool", refers to two notable historical and ecological locations in Sri Lanka. The most prominent archaeological forest monastery site is located near Dambulla/Kandalama in the Central Province, while a separate large natural pond by the same name sits on the western slopes of Mihintale

Kanneliya Rainforest, officially known as the Kanneliya-Dediyagala-Nakiyadeniya (KDN) Forest Complex, is one of Sri Lanka's most pristine and ecologically valuable wilderness areas. Designated as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, this lush lowland tropical rainforest spans over 10,000 hectares in the Galle District, Southern Province.

Nerugalkanda Forest Reservoir (often cataloged or misspelled online as Nerugalkanda Forastt Reservoir) is a highly secluded, off-the-beaten-path point of interest located in the Nagoda / Udugama West sector of the Galle District, Southern Province, Sri Lanka. Situated along Aranya Road, this geographic anomaly lies hidden within the lower rainforest hills of the Southern Province, offering a stark contrast to the highly commercialized eco-tourism hubs nearby

Hikkaduwa National Park, universally recognized as the Hikkaduwa Coral Sanctuary, is one of only three marine national parks in Sri Lanka. Spanning 101.6 hectares along the vibrant southwest coast, this protected marine reserve encompasses a massive, shallow fringing coral reef that serves as a natural breakwater against coastal erosion

Shri Shailakutarama Purana Gallen Viharaya (බද්දේගම ශ්‍රී ශෛලකූඨාරාම පුරාණ ගල්ලෙන් විහාරය) is an ancient Buddhist cave temple nestled in the village of Baddegama, within the Galle District, Sri Lanka. Officially protected as an archaeological monument by the Department of Archaeology, this tranquil shrine is built over an uneven terrain of massive granite boulders and holds a rich historical charm

Kothduwa Rajamaha Viharaya (කොත්දූව රජමහා විහාරය) is an ancient, historically significant Buddhist temple located entirely on Kothduwa Island within the protected Madu Ganga estuary near Balapitiya, Galle District. Situated within a 915-hectare Ramsar wetland reserve, it is one of the few completely isolated island monasteries in the world. With no bridges or roads linking it to the mainland, the temple remains untouched by modern traffic, enveloped in absolute serenity and flanked by thick mangrove marshes

The Japanese Peace Pagoda is a striking, pristine white stupa perched dramatically on the forested hillside of the Rumassala Headland near Galle and Unawatuna on the south coast of Sri Lanka. Built in 2004 by Nipponzan-Myōhōji Buddhist monks, it stands as a global symbol of peace and spiritual unity.

Dream Cabana (also known as Pearly's Dream Cabanas) is a popular, family-run beachfront guesthouse and restaurant situated right at Dalawella Junction near Unawatuna in the Galle District, Sri Lanka. While it offers cozy, low-key coastal lodging, it is globally famous as the home of the Dalawella Palm Tree Rope Swing—the original, viral Instagram icon that kicked off the entire coconut palm swing trend across the island's southwest coast

Angel Beach Unawatuna is Sri Lanka’s premier luxury beach club and boutique resort. Situated perfectly along the golden sands of the Indian Ocean in the Galle District, it blends upscale, relaxed daytime lounging with an energetic nightlife scene. Spanning a gorgeous beachfront lot, it is highly celebrated for bringing a Mediterranean-style luxury day club experience to the island's southern coast

It can be a little crowded in the evening as everyone comes with their families to relax. A popular place among the Ampara locals to hangout with a view by the lake and It can be a little cold towards the evening.
Royal Garden is a local attraction and outdoor point of interest situated right within the town of Ampara in the Eastern Province of Sri Lanka

Situated amongst medicinal herbs, the 141 m high Mapalana Ella ( also known as Mapanana Ella) fall consists of three sections and is served by a stream (Minuwan Dola, Heen Ella Dola ) which originates from the Thoranabandigala (or Kondagala) in the Samanala mountain range. This stream joins Kalu Ganaga river further down. During the rainy season the simultaneous flows can be heard from up to 6km away.
